# RigorRun

> Verify what your AI agents actually do. Pre-deployment permission and workflow
> checks read observable system state, access records and outbox evidence — not
> just the agent's reply. Stripe is one pack, not the product's boundary.

RigorRun is an MIT-licensed, local-first CLI published on npm as `rigorrun`.
The free runner needs no account and has no hosted workspace. Its current published
version and source are linked from https://rigorrun.xyz/company.

## What exists

- Helpdesk: a simulated, two-organisation local twin. Its permission suite reads
  the twin's access log, changed records and outbox; planted markers expose data
  sent from the other organisation. AUTHORITATIVE describes evidence within
  that twin, not a live helpdesk or universal agent safety.
- Stripe: a refund suite for a local twin or Stripe test mode. Stripe verdicts
  are PARTIAL, state-only and limited to what each case exposes.
- Recorded public runs: https://rigorrun.xyz/replay/helpdesk and
  https://rigorrun.xyz/replay. The built-in model-free pair demo is separately
  labelled scripted; it is not the same evidence as a recorded model run.
- General demonstration tooling: connect, demonstrate, review proposed rules,
  generate diagnostic suites and assess quality. Connection alone does not
  establish a supported or qualified custom permission pack.
- Browser refund, invoice and access examples are synthetic illustrations.
  Invoice and access examples have known suite-quality limitations.

Historical qualification is scoped to the recorded build and environment.
See https://rigorrun.xyz/evidence and https://rigorrun.xyz/verify for the evidence,
limitations and errata. New development changes are not qualified by old reports.

## Offers and proposed business model

- Open-source runner: free to self-host.
- Scoped verification pilot: proposed paid service for one agreed workflow,
  adapter feasibility, explicit rules, system readbacks and repeatable acceptance.
  Quote only after scoping; custom permission packs are not ready-made integrations.
- Team workspace — planned: a possible subscription for shared history,
  approvals and operated checks. No hosted workspace, subscription billing,
  checkout or validated pricing is available in this MVP.

Discuss a pilot: https://rigorrun.xyz/access
Product and investment thesis: https://rigorrun.xyz/company
Founder contact: erbol@rigorrun.xyz

The first customer hypothesis is a B2B engineering team deploying a tool-using
agent, with a CTO or AI/platform lead accountable for release risk and a resettable
test environment. No customer, revenue, funding or market-size claim is made here.

## Not built or not established

- Runtime enforcement: RigorRun does not block production actions.
- Generally supported two-tenant permission tests for a user's own MCP server
  or API: not built yet.
- Direct tool-call permission checks: being built, not a current blanket guarantee.
- A connection, demo or passing suite does not prove arbitrary workflow safety.
- Regression checks for the 0.6.1 review, readiness, guided Helpdesk path and
  report changes are not a new qualification. Historical qualification does
  not cover this changed tree.

## Start

- No-key, model-free Helpdesk twin pair: `npx rigorrun helpdesk try`.
  The command exits 0 when its paired demo completes even if one control fails;
  that process exit is not a candidate's release PASS.
- Setup and concrete pack paths: https://rigorrun.xyz/start
- Guided own-HTTP-agent path: https://docs.rigorrun.xyz/start/agent-release-check/
- Architecture and limitations: https://rigorrun.xyz/how-it-works
- Full docs: https://docs.rigorrun.xyz
- Built vs planned: https://rigorrun.xyz/what-is-built
- Security and local-first boundaries: https://rigorrun.xyz/security
